title: The 10 Best Benchtop Drill Presses
subtitle: 8-inch to 12-inch benchtop drill presses for straight, repeatable holes in wood and metal, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A drill press drills dead-square holes to a set depth, every time, which a handheld drill can't. We ranked 10 benchtop best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (variable speed without moving belts, a laser crosshair, a work light and a digital speed readout). The big split is size: 8-inch machines with 1/2-inch chucks for small parts and hobby work, and 12-inch machines with 5/8-inch chucks and over 3 inches of spindle travel for furniture and metal. They run from about $125 for WOODSKIL's 8-inch to $736 for JET's 12-inch.

avoid.name: BACHIN Bench Drill Stand 710W Mini Electric Bench Drilling Machine, 6-Speed, 0-2800RPM
avoid.flag: Power and speed claims contradict each other
avoid.verdict: A mini drill on a stand whose own numbers don't add up. For about $35 more, the WOODSKIL DP-8 is a real 8-inch cast iron press with a stated swing and spindle travel.
reasons: It claims 710 watts but lists 3.23 amps at 110 volts. That's about 355 watts drawn from the wall, half the headline figure.
The listing calls it '6-speed' and '0-2800RPM variable' at the same time, and the spec table gives its dimensions as 1 x 1 x 1 inch.
It lists no swing, spindle travel, or warranty, the numbers you need to know what a drill press can actually drill.

buyers_guide.q: What does swing mean on a drill press?
buyers_guide.a: Swing is twice the distance from the column to the center of the chuck. An 8-inch swing can drill the center of an 8-inch-wide board; a 12-inch swing handles 12 inches.

buyers_guide.q: How much spindle travel do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Spindle travel is how deep you can drill in one plunge. 2 inches covers most hobby and metal work. For deep holes in table legs or thick stock, look for 3 inches or more, like the JET JWDP-12.

Belt-speed presses work fine, but you open the top and move a belt to change speed. Variable-speed presses change with a lever or dial, which matters when you switch between small bits, Forstner bits and metal often.

buyers_guide.q: What speed should I drill metal at?
buyers_guide.a: Slower than wood, and slower still for bigger bits. Large bits in steel want the bottom of the range (500-700 rpm), so a low minimum speed matters more than a high maximum.

buyers_guide.q: Should I bolt a benchtop drill press down?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. They're top-heavy, and JET's listing says its press must be bolted down. Bolt it to a sturdy bench or stand before use.
